evidence.title: Adding Plausible to Wix
evidence.text:
You can use the **Custom Code** feature to add Plausible Analytics tracking code to your Wix website the same way you would add Google Analytics code or any other JavaScript code.

Site-wide JavaScript code injection is a premium Wix feature so you need to upgrade your Wix account to a paid subscription plan.

* In your site's dashboard, click on **Settings**, and under **Development & Integrations** click on **Custom Code**.

* Click the **+ Add Custom Code** button in the top right.

* Paste your Plausible tracking code, give it a name, choose which pages to add the code to (**All Pages**), select **Load code once per visit** (read more about this here), select **Head** as the place for the code and click the **Apply** button.

Now you can go to your website and verify whether Plausible Analytics script has been added and to your Plausible Analytics account to see whether the stats are being tracked. See here how to verify the integration.

question: i run a mediawiki for our team. how do i add plausible to it?
reference_answer: Download and activate the Plausible extension: clone the octfx mediawiki-extension-Plausible repository into your extensions/Plausible folder, add wfLoadExtension( 'Plausible' ); to LocalSettings.php and configure it as needed.

Add wfLoadExtension( 'Plausible' ); to LocalSettings.php
answer:
You can add Plausible Analytics to your MediaWiki instance by downloading and activating the Plausible extension [1]. First, clone the extension to your `/extensions` folder:

```shell
git clone https://github.com/octfx/mediawiki-extension-Plausible extensions/Plausible
```

Then, add `wfLoadExtension( 'Plausible' );` to your `LocalSettings.php` file [1].

question: I added up the visitors in my Top Pages report and it's way more than the total unique visitors at the top. Is my data wrong?
reference_answer: Your data isn't wrong. Unique visitors counts each visitor once for the selected period, while Top Pages counts visitors separately for each page, so someone who visits several pages appears in several rows. Adding those rows therefore gives a higher number than the total.
key_facts: Unique visitors counts each visitor once for the period
Top Pages counts visitors separately per page
A visitor who views several pages appears in several rows
answer: Your data is not wrong; it is common for the numbers in your Top Pages report to not add up to the total unique visitors [1]. The Top Pages report counts visitors separately for each page, so a single visitor who views multiple pages will be counted in the rows for each of those pages [1]. Because visitors are not limited to a single pageview or action, adding up these individual rows will result in a higher number than the dashboard's total unique visitors [1].

The **Top Pages** report counts visitors separately for each page, so someone who visits several pages appears in several rows.

evidence.title: Dashboard FAQ
evidence.text:
It's common to see that the numbers in your dashboard aren't _adding up_. The **Unique visitors** metric counts each visitor once for the selected period. The **Top Pages** report counts visitors separately for each page, so someone who visits several pages appears in several rows. Adding those rows can therefore give a higher number than the dashboard's total unique visitors.

Plausible dashboard with total unique visitors above a Top Pages report listing visitors for each page

This happens because visitors can view more than a single page or trigger more than a single custom event on your site. Imagine a single visitor triggering two pageviews: `/page1` and `/page2`. In this case your Plausible dashboard would show 1 unique visitor in total. However, the **Top Pages** tab would show one unique visitor for `/page1` and one unique visitor for `/page2`.

This is why adding up unique visitor numbers and comparing them to the total is misleading. Since visitors aren't limited to a single pageview or action on your site, you shouldn't expect these numbers to be equal.

There's another situation where differences might occur. If you manually tally the unique visitors for each day in a month, you may not get the same result as the number of unique visitors you see in the report for that month. This discrepancy is due to sessions that overlap with our daily reset. Consider this: If someone visits your site 5 minutes before our daily reset and they continue being engaged with your site until 5 minutes after the reset, their session will count as one unique visitor on each of the two days. However, in the monthly view, that visitor will be counted as one unique visitor only.

question: I'm A/B testing my pricing page and the CR column in the properties report looks totally off. Is something broken?
reference_answer: Nothing is broken. You should ignore the CR column in that report because it's calculated against all the visitors to your site, not against each variant's visitors. Use the Visitors column instead, first unfiltered to see who saw each variant and then filtered by your goal to see who converted.
key_facts: Ignore the CR column in the Properties report
CR is calculated against all site visitors, not each variant's visitors
Use the Visitors column, filtered by the goal, to see conversions per variant
answer: The CR column in the properties report is calculated against all the visitors to your site, not against each variant's visitors, so you should ignore it in this report [1]. To see the correct conversion data, filter your dashboard by the goal you are testing [1]. The column will then show how many visitors converted with each variant [1].

Then filter your dashboard by the goal you're testing. The same column now shows how many visitors converted with each variant.

evidence.title: Measure A/B tests with Plausible
evidence.text:
At the bottom of your dashboard, in the **Goals** section, open the **Properties** tab and choose `variant`. The **Visitors** column shows how many visitors saw each variant.

Then filter your dashboard by the goal you're testing. The same column now shows how many visitors converted with each variant. Ignore the **CR** (conversion rate) column in this report. It's calculated against all the visitors to your site, not against each variant's visitors.

answer: When configuring your script tag on Vercel, the `src` and `endpoint` attributes must match the `source` values you defined in your `vercel.json` file [1].

```html

<script>
```

question: My accountant wants a PDF of last month's invoice. Where do I find it?
reference_answer: In your account settings, scroll down in the Subscription section to the list of invoices and open one in a new tab. Use your browser's Print command and choose Save as PDF.
key_facts: Invoices are listed in the Subscription section
Open the invoice then Print > Save as PDF
answer: You can access your past invoices by logging into your Plausible account and opening your settings [1]. In the Subscription section, you will find a list of all your invoices [1]. Select the invoice you need to open it in a new browser tab, then use your browser's Print command and select Save as PDF to save a copy [1][2].

evidence.title: View and save your invoices
evidence.text:
Our payment processor Paddle sends an invoice by email automatically after each payment. You can also view past invoices from your Plausible account. Paddle doesn't issue credit notes or receipts for refunds, so a refund has no separate document.

Log in to your Plausible account. In the top right menu, click your account name and open the settings. Scroll down in the **Subscription** section to see a list of all invoices. Select an invoice to open it in a new browser tab.

To save a PDF copy, use your browser's **Print** command and select **Save as PDF** as the destination.

Invoice list in Plausible settings

## Add your company address and VAT number

Open any invoice from Paddle and click **Add address & VAT Number**. Paddle handles VAT and sales taxes. If you provide a valid VAT ID, no VAT will be charged on future payments. UK businesses are the exception: Paddle still charges UK VAT, which you can reclaim on your VAT return. Your company details and VAT number are added to invoices from then on. Other invoices that were already issued stay as they were. When Paddle refunds the VAT on a payment after accepting your VAT number, it doesn't send a separate credit note. Instead, it reissues that payment's invoice without VAT, and the reissued invoice is the one for your records. More on Paddle's VAT handling →

## Change your billing address

Open any invoice and click **Edit business address** to update your address.

Changing the **country** on an existing subscription isn't possible due to tax regulations. To switch countries, cancel your subscription a day or two before your next renewal, then subscribe again right away from the same account with the new country (see How do I change the country on my subscription?). No data is lost in this process.

evidence.title: Billing FAQ
evidence.text:
Paddle (our payment processor) emails you an invoice automatically after each payment. You can also open past invoices from the **Subscription** section of your settings. Paddle opens each invoice in a browser tab, so use your browser's **Print** command and select **Save as PDF** to save a copy. See View and save your invoices.

The invoice email goes to your Paddle email address, which may differ from your Plausible login email. To change it, contact us with your current and desired invoice email.
